Minerals are naturally occurring inorganic substances with a specific chemical composition and a crystalline structure. They can be classified into two main types: metallic and non-metallic minerals.

Metallic minerals can be further divided into ferrous and non-ferrous minerals. Ferrous minerals, such as iron ore and manganese, contain iron. Non-ferrous minerals, like gold, silver, and copper, do not contain iron but may contain other metals.

Non-metallic minerals, on the other hand, do not contain metals. Examples of non-metallic minerals include limestone, mica, gypsum, and mineral fuels like coal and petroleum.

There are over 3,000 known types of minerals, but only about 100 are considered ore minerals, from which minerals can be mined. Minerals can be extracted through various methods, including mining, drilling, and quarrying.
